section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbat Parshat Bo,
8 Shevat,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section notes that the maamar is a discourse given by the Rebbe.
section.t: (A discourse)

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the concept of the Shechinah descending through the righteous, the purpose of the Mishkan, and the service of offerings.
section.t: "I have come to My garden, My sister, My bride."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Admor of the hillula, brings
[in the maamar
that was given by him for the day of his histalkus, Shabbat Parshat Bo, 10 Shevat,
the teaching of the Midrash:
"To My garden, to My orchard, to the place that was My primary dwelling initially,"
that the primary dwelling of the Shechinah was in the lower realms,
but through undesirable matters during the course of seven generations, they removed the Shechinah from below upward until the seventh heaven,
and afterward the righteous arose and drew down the Shechinah from above downward,
and the beginning of the drawing down was from Avraham,
"Avraham was one,"
who brought it down from the seventh heaven to the sixth, etc., until Moshe, who is the seventh, and all sevenths are beloved,
brought it down below to earth.
And this is why the making of the Mishkan was through Moshe
(specifically),
for the concept of the Mishkan is as it is stated,
"And they shall make Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell in their midst,"
that through "And they shall make Me a Sanctuary," there is brought about "And I will dwell" below, within the children of Israel and within the world,
for from the indwelling of the Shechinah that was in the Holy Temple, the revelation was drawn through the windows that are "transparent yet sealed"
throughout the entire world.
And all this was accomplished through the service of Israel, and as our Sages, of blessed memory, precisely stated,
"It does not say 'within it,' but rather 'within them'—within each and every one of Israel,"
that through the service of Israel
(and "Your people are all righteous")
there is brought about "And I will dwell" in the Mishkan, and through this, in the entire world.
And this is [the meaning of] "The righteous shall inherit the land and dwell upon it forever,"
that "the righteous shall inherit the land," which is the Land of Life
(the Garden of Eden),
because they cause to dwell and draw down
the aspect of "Shochein" (the Indwelling One),
the aspect of "Ad" (eternity),
the aspect of the "Sovev" (the Encompassing),
so that it will be revealed below through the service of Torah and mitzvos.
And as it is stated,
"I made the earth and created man upon it,"
that this
[is what is meant by] "I made the earth"—it is for the sake of man, and the creation of man is for the sake of "Bereisi" (I created him), which in gematria equals 613,
meaning that through the fulfillment of the 613 mitzvos, the intention of creation is completed—that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place in the lower realms.
And this is why one of the services that was in the Temple was the matter of the service of the offerings,
for the service of the offerings is a spiritual service within the soul of man,
and as the Alter Rebbe precisely explains
regarding the verse,
"When a man from among you brings an offering," etc., that the offering must be from you, literally,
from the animal soul within man,
and it says about this, "from the cattle and from the flock,"
these are the specific levels that exist in the animal soul
(and as explained in many places
regarding the matter of ox, sheep, and goat).
And this service was in the Temple,
for all ascents are through the Temple.
For just as all the draw-downs are through the Temple,
and as above, that the drawing down of the Shechinah into the world was through the "transparent yet sealed" windows of the Temple,
so too, the ascents from below upward are through the Temple,
therefore, when one prays, he should direct his intention toward the Holy Temple.
And based on this, he explains there why the Mishkan was made of acacia wood,
for the primary service of man is the matter of subjugation and transformation of darkness into light,
and therefore the Mishkan was made of acacia wood,
which is an expression of foolishness,
the transformation of the foolishness of the side of impurity that is below the intellectual realm,
[for] a person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of foolishness enters into him,
into the foolishness of holiness that is above the intellectual realm.
